Join us for a socially distant, mask-wearing march for justice.     March for...    * Racial equality. Black Lives Matter. Stand with our fellow BIOPC citizens.  * Women's rights to our own bodies.  * Access to voting for all, for a fairer democracy.  * Fair, affordable healthcare for all.  * Our planet and the environment. Believe in science.  * Equal rights for LGBTQIA+ citizens.  * Freedom of religion, including freedom from religion.  * Immigrants' and refugees' rights. Families belong together.    The Women's March movement is led by women, including trans women, genderqueer women, and non-binary people who are significantly female-identified. People of all genders are invited to participate in and help organize our socially distanced Arlington Women's March.    === Schedule for Our March ===    * 2:00pm. Stand vigil on any location on Massachusetts Avenue in Arlington, on the sidewalk. Stay 6 feet or more from other protestors. Allow access to sidewalk ramps, and keep clear of business entrances.    * 2:15pm. Begin marching toward Arlington Center, while maintaining social distance (6’+). Arlington Center is located at the intersection of Mass Ave (Rt3) and Mystic St (Rt60), Arlington.    *As you approach Arlington Center, use your best judgment to maintain social distance. If it is safe to do so, walk past Arlington Town Hall at 730 Mass Ave*, then cross the street. Then, march toward your original locations.    * Please note that Arlington Town Hall sidewalk is currently under construction.  https://www.arlingtonma.gov/.../Comp.../News/News/10536/3977    * There may be pedestrian congestion near Town Hall. Keep marching as much as possible! Let’s minimize congestion, pass by each other quickly when necessary, and avoid close proximity for a prolonged period of time. Our priority is to march for human rights and social justice while keeping everybody safe from potential COVID-19 transmission.    * The march concludes once you return to your initial location. You may continue to stand vigil until 3:30pm, as a show of solidarity.    Thank you for fighting for social justice.    === https://fb.me/e/1wECpcbzL ===

This will be an opportunity to stand together against the destructive agenda of Donald Trump and those who support him.      In this time of national distress, we need to come together in supporting the highest ideals of the United States of America.   At this time, “Liberty and Justice for ALL” finally needs to mean every human being.       Please join us in celebrating Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg, standing against the dictatorship/theocracy that Trump supporters want, and standing with each other to declare that we are not going back.      The event will be on the Capitol Steps.  I had initially reserved the Fountain Plaza for its ease of access but the folks in charge said with the number of people (155 and counting!) we would be better on the steps. The Capitol Steps is on the Commonwealth Avenue side (west side right at the intersection of State Street and Third Street) of the Pennsylvania Capitol.   Parking will be free around the park on the other side of the capitol, Soldiers’ Grove, across Commonwealth Avenue, across from the fountain.  Stop and see the fountain anyway since it is dyed a lovely pink for Breast Cancer Awareness Month.    otherwise, parking will be for a fee on the streets and garages.  Info is here: https://parkharrisburg.com/      The steps are a very good venue, getting plenty of exposure but they are not conducive to folks with disabilities, being historical and not ADA compliant.  The sidewalk does come right up to them at the bottom.   The top drive is limited access for security reasons.      I am not going to have portable toilets because of the relatively short duration of the event.   Please pee before you come.  There are restaurants nearby but none will welcome the public just wandering in.  But they are great for a lunch!  The capitol will be open through the entrance at the top of the steps, but again, this is not accessible for disabled folks.  The PA capitol is gorgeous.      I am accessing a decent sound system so we can be heard.  We are looking for speakers. Please contact me.     Mask wearing and social distancing will be enforced.    Since it is close to Halloween, wear a costume of your favorite unruly woman.  :)  As for what to bring: a sign if you'd like:  nothing contraband;  a cushion of blanket if you'd like to sit on the steps or the walls around them, a couple places can also handle a foldable chair;  a hat if you are sensitive to the sun, something to drink if you'd like. notes: Women's March; Women's March Coalition of East TN - Day of Action; The Women's March Coalition of Knoxville in conjunction with our community partners, Indivisible East Tennessee, and the Knox County Democratic Party, will participate in the Women's March national and statewide day of action with a local event.    Participants need to mask up and will be required to follow social distancing precautions as we continue to keep one another safe during the pandemic . There are also remote options available for those who are not comfortable with an in person event.    Locally, we will be having a two part approach to our day of action! At 10:00 a.m., we will be assembling downtown for a short rally at Krutch Park which will highlight what is at stake this election. Guest speakers will cover topics such as the Affordable Care Act, marriage equality, women's health and reproductive freedom and information on voting.    Next, we will march to the polls (City County Building, an early voting site) so that anyone who would like to may cast their vote early. (Please make sure you bring a photo ID and that you are able to cover up/remove any campaign related paraphernalia which is not allowed at the election poll site.)  After marching back to the rally site, we will then disburse for the second part of the Day of Action...    Our local, state and federal campaigns are down to the wire and need volunteers to text, phone bank, conduct literature drops, canvass, and deliver yard signs. We want to plug in the energy and people power of the Women's March to our area progressive campaigns.    Campaigns are currently organizing their individual Day of Action events for the afternoon of the 17th. They will be creating Facebook events for their actions and we will be linking those in the event page as they become available.  (You will be able to pick the way in which they would like to participate and which of the candidates you would like to support.)    We have rallied, marched and carried signs and while that is great for awareness and visibility, we wanted to find a way to make a direct impact.  So, join us on Saturday, October 17th to cast your vote with your friends, loved ones, and fellow Women's March resisters and then spend the afternoon volunteering on a campaign to make positive change!

After getting inspiration from many of our favorite femme candidates and community leaders, we will get to work either canvassing on the issues, phone banking or sign waiving. Folks will be grouped and assigned locations, and we will talk to women about why they need to vote and who they need to vote for in support of our ability to thrive. We'll have our 2020 "Breaking Our Chains" shirts beautifully designed by LeoArt available for our "marchers" as supplies last. Face masks are mandatory. Please wear comfortable shoes and be prepared for Miami weather (bring sunglasses, a hat, sunscreen and rain gear). We will also have a phone banking station and sign waving stations.    We're happy to have you at our Wynwood (base camp) location, but you can also host your own event at your chosen location that same day to bring the march to your community!
